analysis.investment_thesis: Firstsource is a decent BPO/IT services business with consistent but unspectacular growth (~10.6% revenue CAGR), yet it fails both Magic Formula screens — Earnings Yield of only ~6.5% (EV ≈ INR 19,095 Cr vs. EBIT of INR 1,238 Cr) and ROCE of 15.4% fall well short of the >12% and >25% thresholds I require. At EV/EBITDA of 15.5x and P/E of 24x, the market is pricing in a business quality that the returns on capital simply don't justify.
key_strengths: Consistent OCF generation — 5/5 years positive, with INR 701 Cr OCF in FY25 and operating income CAGR of 13.4% over 9 years
Diversified revenue across Healthcare, BFS, and CMT verticals reduces client concentration risk
Strong promoter holding at 53.66% with meaningful DII ownership (25.49%) signals institutional confidence
key_risks: Debt surged to INR 2,569 Cr in FY25 (from INR 1,526 Cr in FY24), likely acquisition-driven, while cash collapsed to just INR 13 Cr — a dangerously thin liquidity cushion
Finance costs nearly tripled from INR 61 Cr (FY16) to INR 184 Cr (FY25), compressing the earnings available to equity holders and eating into ROIC
FCF declining sharply — from INR 806 Cr (FY21) to INR 477 Cr (FY25) — while capex jumped to INR 241 Cr in FY25 vs. ~INR 85 Cr historically, suggesting a capital-intensity inflection
red_flags: FY25 Investing CF of -744 Cr suggests a large unannounced or recent acquisition, funded by doubling debt — integration risk is real and unquantifiable from available data
Cash balance of only INR 13 Cr against INR 2,569 Cr of total debt is a structural concern if revenue growth decelerates
Net profit CAGR (9.6%) lagging revenue CAGR (10.6%) and operating income CAGR (13.4%) means margin expansion is not flowing to the bottom line — financing costs are the culprit
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Firstsource: EBIT of INR 1,238 Cr against an Enterprise Value of ~INR 19,095 Cr (market cap INR 16,539 Cr + debt INR 2,569 Cr – cash INR 13 Cr) yields an Earnings Yield of just 6.5% — barely above my 6% floor and well below the 12%+ I find attractive. ROCE of 15.4% is adequate for a labor-intensive BPO but nowhere near the 25%+ that characterizes a genuinely high-quality business deserving a premium multiple. Both Magic Formula metrics are in the mediocre range simultaneously, which is the worst outcome — neither cheap nor exceptional.

The FY25 data introduces new concerns. Debt nearly doubled YoY and capex tripled to INR 241 Cr, yet FCF dropped to INR 477 Cr — the lowest since FY20. A business that grows revenue at 10.6% CAGR while letting debt balloon and FCF shrink is consuming, not creating, shareholder value per rupee deployed. At P/E 24x and EV/EBITDA 15.5x, the market is paying a growth premium for what is, by ROIC metrics, an average-quality BPO franchise. I'd need to see the stock at closer to 12-14x EBITDA with ROCE sustainably above 20% before the Magic Formula lights turn green.
